transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because since I moved into this busted-up room, I’ve been on edge. I’m up half the night dealing with leaks or the heat, then I’m dragging into work late and messing up things I normally handle. I’ve been snapping at people too.
How long ago did you move into this room?
About a month now—started not long after I moved into that room in Bridgeport.
Aside from feeling on edge, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?
I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently sad or hopeless. Mostly I’ve just been stressed out and wound up about the room.
Before you moved into this room, did you have any trouble with your sleep?
No, not that I can remember. I was sleeping pretty normally before I moved in there.
Besides snapping at people, have you gotten into any physical fights, damaged property, or had any trouble with the law?
No, nothing like that. I’ve just been snapping at people more than I normally would.

inference_history.note: Patient presents with anxiety, sleep disturbance, irritability, and occupational impairment following a clear environmental stressor (moving into a substandard living situation), suggesting Adjustment disorder (F43.2), Generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1), Depressive episode (F32), or primary sleep disturbance (F51.0).
Ruled out F41.1 because symptom duration is only about one month following an identifiable stressor, which does not meet the typical 6-month duration requirement for generalized anxiety disorder.
